answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, a smart-contract bond is created for each identity, locking its own refundable bond. This makes multiple identities costly, as each must pay for their own bond. Slash payments only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, like a walnut cracking under pressure. In a digital grove, this ensures a single, authentic identity, while in a vast canyon of transactions, it prevents malicious actors from masquerading as multiple identities.
